tools.name: get_timeline_state
tools.description: Get the full timeline state including all tracks, clips, and composition settings.

tools.name: get_media_library
tools.description: Get all imported media files available for use on the timeline.

tools.name: get_clip_at_time
tools.description: Get the clip at a specific playhead time position.

time.description: Time position in seconds to query.

tools.name: get_selected_clip
tools.description: Get the currently selected/active clip and its properties.

tools.name: add_clip
tools.description: Add a media file to the timeline at a specific position.

media_file_id.description: ID of the media file from the library to add.

track_id.description: Target track ID. If omitted, adds to the first video track (V1).

timeline_start.description: Start time on the timeline in seconds. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: remove_clip
tools.description: Remove a clip from the timeline by its ID.

clip_id.description: ID of the clip to remove. If omitted, removes the currently selected clip.

tools.name: trim_clip
tools.description: Trim a clip's source start or end point. Adjusts which portion of the source media is shown.

clip_id.description: ID of the clip to trim. If omitted, uses the currently selected clip.

source_start.description: New source start time in seconds. Trims from the beginning.

source_end.description: New source end time in seconds. Trims from the end.

tools.name: move_clip
tools.description: Move a clip to a new position on the timeline, optionally to a different track.

clip_id.description: ID of the clip to move. If omitted, uses the currently selected clip.

timeline_start.description: New start time on the timeline in seconds.

track_id.description: Target track ID. If omitted, stays on the current track.

tools.name: apply_effect
tools.description: Apply ONE visual or audio effect from a fixed registry to a clip. Use this for simple, single-effect requests (e.g. 'add sepia', 'fade out the last 1s', 'rotate 15 degrees'). For requests that combine multiple FFmpeg filters, use custom filters not in this registry, or need a non-trivial filter graph (e.g. 'crush the blacks and add film grain', 'apply a teal-and-orange LUT then sharpen'), prefer `compose_recipe` — it can reach the full FFmpeg filter catalog via `list_filters` / `describe_filter`. Note: only `fade_in`, `fade_out`, `crop`, `vignette`, and CSS-mappable filters (blur, brightness, contrast, saturation, grayscale, sepia, hue_rotate) render in the live preview; other effects only become visible on export.

clip_id.description: ID of the clip to apply the effect to. If omitted, uses the currently selected clip.

parameters.description: Effect-specific parameters as key-value pairs. Keys correspond to the effect's parameter IDs.

tools.name: update_effect_param
tools.description: Update a parameter on an already-applied effect.

clip_id.description: ID of the clip. If omitted, uses the currently selected clip.

applied_effect_id.description: ID of the applied effect instance on the clip.

parameters.description: Updated parameter values as key-value pairs.

tools.name: remove_effect
tools.description: Remove an applied effect from a clip. Use this to undo an apply_effect call — pass the applied_effect_id returned by apply_effect.

clip_id.description: ID of the clip the effect is on. If omitted, uses the currently selected clip.

applied_effect_id.description: ID of the applied effect instance on the clip (returned by apply_effect).

tools.name: toggle_effect
tools.description: Enable or disable an applied effect without removing it. Useful for previewing 'before/after' or temporarily suppressing an effect.

clip_id.description: ID of the clip the effect is on. If omitted, uses the currently selected clip.

applied_effect_id.description: ID of the applied effect instance on the clip.

enabled.description: True to enable the effect, false to disable it.

tools.name: list_filter_categories
tools.description: List all FFmpeg filter categories with their filter counts. Use this to discover what kinds of filters are available before browsing specific categories.

tools.name: list_filters
tools.description: List available FFmpeg filters, optionally filtered by category or keyword search. Returns filter names, types, and descriptions.

category.description: Category ID to filter by (e.g. 'color', 'blur', 'transform'). Get valid IDs from list_filter_categories.

query.description: Keyword to search filter names and descriptions.

tools.name: describe_filter
tools.description: Get detailed info about a specific FFmpeg filter including all its parameters, types, defaults, and value ranges.

filter_name.description: Name of the FFmpeg filter to describe (e.g. 'eq', 'hue', 'gblur').

tools.name: compose_recipe
tools.description: SEED a new FFmpeg filter recipe on a clip that has none. If the clip ALREADY has a recipe, this tool errors — use append_to_recipe for additive asks ("also add grain", "a bit warmer") and refine_recipe ONLY when the user explicitly asks to simplify/redo the look. WORKFLOW: (0) try search_recipe_templates first — a seed template may already match the ask. (1) discover real filters with list_creative_filters (curated, with worked examples) or list_filters/describe_filter — do not invent filter names from memory. (2) Build nodes with filter+params (or raw for expression-heavy filters like curves). (3) Connections link input → first → … → last → output. The recipe is structurally validated AND dry-run through FFmpeg before attaching — on error, fix and retry. NOT in stock FFmpeg: vibrance, tonemap; substitutes: vibrance → eq+colorchannelmixer, warm/cool → curves/colorbalance. The live preview re-renders automatically a moment after the recipe attaches. Pass the user's ask as `prompt` so the look is saved to the learned template cache.

clip_id.description: ID of the clip to attach the recipe to. If omitted, uses the currently selected clip.

recipe.description: Recipe object with 'nodes' array (each node has 'id', 'filter', 'params' or 'raw') and 'connections' array (each has 'from' and 'to' node IDs, using 'input'/'output' for endpoints).

prompt.description: The user's originating ask, verbatim-ish (e.g. "dreamy vintage sunset look"). Recorded in the revision log and the learned template cache.

tools.name: validate_recipe
tools.description: Validate a recipe by compiling it to an FFmpeg filter string and running a dry-run. Returns the compiled filter string on success, or an error describing what's wrong.

recipe.description: Recipe object to validate (same format as compose_recipe).

tools.name: append_to_recipe
tools.description: ADD nodes onto a clip's EXISTING recipe — the default tool for additive asks ("also add grain", "now make it warmer", "add a vignette on top"). Appends are strictly additive: existing nodes are NEVER modified or removed; your fragment is spliced between the current graph's end and the output. Fragment semantics: nodes = NEW nodes only (fresh ids — use get_recipe to see existing ids); connections may reference only the new node ids plus 'input' (= the END of the existing recipe) and 'output'. Omit connections to simply chain the new nodes in order. The MERGED graph is validated + FFmpeg dry-run before committing — on error the existing recipe is untouched; fix the fragment and retry. The live preview re-renders automatically.

clip_id.description: Target clip. If omitted, uses the currently selected clip.

fragment.description: { nodes: RecipeNode[], connections?: RecipeConnection[] }. New nodes only; 'input' means the existing recipe's output.

prompt.description: The user's ask motivating this append — recorded in the revision log.

tools.name: refine_recipe
tools.description: REWRITE a clip's recipe wholesale — compaction or redo. Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to simplify, clean up, tone down overall, or redo the look (e.g. "simplify this", "too much, start the grade over"). For additive changes use append_to_recipe instead. Provide the FULL replacement graph. Prior revisions are carried forward in the log and the prior graph remains recoverable via edit history. Validated + dry-run before committing.

clip_id.description: Target clip. If omitted, uses the currently selected clip.

recipe.description: The complete replacement recipe: { nodes, connections }.

prompt.description: Why the rewrite (e.g. "user asked to simplify").

tools.name: get_recipe
tools.description: Inspect a clip's current recipe: nodes (with the revision that added each), connections, the compiled FFmpeg filter string, and the revision log (compose/append/refine history with prompts). Call this BEFORE append_to_recipe to learn existing node ids and see how the look was built.

clip_id.description: Target clip. If omitted, uses the currently selected clip.

tools.name: search_recipe_templates
tools.description: Fuzzy-search the recipe template library (shipped seed looks + looks learned from this user's past sessions) by name/tags/description. Try this FIRST when the user asks for a named/stylistic look ("vhs", "teal and orange", "film noir", "dreamy") — apply a match via compose_recipe (verbatim or tweaked) instead of building from scratch.

query.description: Style keywords, e.g. "vhs retro", "warm film sunset".

tools.name: list_creative_filters
tools.description: Curated catalog of high-value stock FFmpeg filters with what each is FOR and a worked example string (curves, colorbalance, lut3d, noise, tblend, lagfun, zoompan, the split+blend intensity-dial pattern, …). Ground your recipe composition here instead of guessing filter names/params.

tools.name: list_luts
tools.description: List available 3D LUT (.cube) files — shipped looks (teal_orange, warm_film, cool_noir, vaporwave_pink, bleach_bypass) plus any user-supplied LUTs. Returns name + absolute path. Apply at full strength with a node {filter:'lut3d', params:{file:'<path>'}}… BUT paths contain characters FFmpeg parses, so prefer a raw node: raw: "lut3d='<path>'". For partial strength (the pro 'intensity slider'), use the split+blend pattern as ONE raw node: raw: "split[__a][__b];[__b]lut3d='<path>'[__g];[__a][__g]blend=all_expr='A*(1-0.6)+B*0.6'" (0.6 = 60% intensity).
